# SPEC — the behavioural single source of truth

This document is the repository's behavioural SSOT: every enforced norm, gate class, and workflow contract is homed here. `MISSION.md` states direction; this SPEC states behavior — MISSION content is cited, never restated.

## 0. Intent and scope

This section states what the SPEC governs, its subordination to `MISSION.md`, and the reading conventions — the marker-delimited table of contents exists so readers take targeted section reads instead of loading the whole document.

## 1. Work norms

This section states the standard flow every change rides — issue → branch → draft PR → review-gated merge — and the Doc → Test → Code work order with its strict and relaxed conditions, including the per-PR changelog-fragment discipline.

## 2. Artifact hierarchy and lifecycle

This section states the issue types and their lifecycle states (proposed → active → closed), the PR-as-living-doc contract, and the evidence discipline durable artifacts must satisfy.

## 3. Enforcement-layer architecture

This section states the first-class design constraint — pi provides no built-in permission system, so the shell's enforcement layer is the only safety net — and enumerates the gate classes across three tiers: in-process pi-extension gates, the local git-hook tier, and CI gates.

## 4. Substrate and install contract

This section states how shell assets install into a repository: target-parameterized, homed in shell-owned namespaces that collide with no other tooling's, and landed through PR-based installs.

## 5. Cross-cutting contracts

This section states the contracts that bind every section: self-contained artifacts, graceful degradation for best-effort automations, and explicit activation conditions for gates that sleep until their subject exists.

## 6. Self-hosting milestone

This section states the criterion for the point at which this repository's own development runs under the shell it ships.
